raw_answer_text:
A1: It is broadcast to every station on the Ethernet segment (broadcast address FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF).
A2: It lacks the mapping of the target's IP (protocol) address to its hardware (MAC) address in its ARP cache/table.
A3: It stores the requesting host's IP (protocol) address together with its hardware (MAC) address.
A4: No, non-target hosts silently discard the request (though they may update their own cache with the sender's mapping) without sending a reply.
A5: The reply is sent directly (unicast) to the requesting host, not broadcast.
A6: It stores the target's IP-to-hardware address mapping in its ARP cache/table for future use.
A7: No, obtaining the target's hardware address is precisely the purpose of the request; the host only knows the target's protocol (IP) address beforehand.
A8: It merges the sender's address mapping into its table before checking whether the opcode is a request or a reply.
